paragraphs: R' Yehoshua ben Matya. (A tanna mentioned in the Mishnah.)

In [Eduyot 2:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Eduyot.2.5), three matters were brought before Rabbi Yishmael. He gave no ruling of either prohibition or permission, and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Matya explained them. Yuḥasin says that he lived at the time R' Elazar ben Azarya was appointed. But this provides little proof, since Eduyot mentions tannaim from the preceding generation as well as from later generations.[^1]

notes.text: Hyman prints Eduyot, chapter 2, mishnah 2 (פ״ב מ״ב). The matching passage is numbered 2:5 in the named Hebrew edition Torat Emet 357: it gives full Rabbi titles for Yishmael and Yehoshua ben Matya and says that Yishmael gave no ruling of prohibition or permission. The English reference points to that matching passage; Hyman’s printed locator is preserved here. Yuḥasin is the title as cited, without an edition identification or independent collation. The familiar initials ראב״ע are rendered R' Elazar ben Azarya in the context of the appointment, preserving an abbreviated personal title. Hyman’s objection to the chronological inference is unchanged.
